Technical Skills.D5: Practice pathlib/file I/O, dictionaries and data classes for record metadata, structured logging, Git commits, and running a minimal test suite.
Technical Skills.F5: A small script reads a benign fixture, validates required fields, and records a reproducible run.
Technical Skills.G5: Python standard-library docs; pytest getting-started guide; project environment tooling docs.

Technical Skills.D6: Learn the difference between FASTA sequence-only records and annotated GenBank records; inspect feature tables, coordinates, strand, qualifiers, and missing/ambiguous annotations using benign examples.
Technical Skills.F6: Explain the schema and manually verify a few parsed records against their public annotations.
Technical Skills.G6: Biopython SeqIO and GenBank feature documentation; basic molecular biology quickstart recommended in the proposal.

Technical Skills.D7: Practice calling a pretrained model without fine-tuning, tracking model/version/configuration, respecting input limits, saving outputs, and distinguishing model coverage from label agreement.
Technical Skills.F7: One repeatable paired run produces comparable outputs and a short metric summary.
Technical Skills.G7: Documentation for the selected model/library; scikit-learn metric documentation if classification metrics fit the label design.

Technical Skills.D8: Review unit/integration tests, regression testing, CLI argument design, pinned environments, and interpreting precision/recall/F1 or other metrics only when labels support them.
Technical Skills.F8: A clean-checkout demo runs from documented instructions and reports limitations clearly.
Technical Skills.G8: pytest docs; Python packaging/CLI documentation; reproducibility checklist.

Technical Skills.B11: Basic molecular biology literacy (CDS, promoters, terminators, tags, linkers, backbones) and comfort with command-line tools/environment management are useful throughout. Familiarity with BLAST/DIAMOND/HMMER is background context, not a separate MVP workstream unless the chosen evaluation requires a baseline.

MVP Criteria.A2: Use this tab in Week 1 to agree what 'done' means; revisit in Week 4. Keep stretch goals from displacing the core deliverable.

MVP Criteria.C5: Accepts documented public benign construct records in the selected format(s) and validates them.

MVP Criteria.C6: Emits normalized, model-ready units with stable parent-child identifiers and provenance.

MVP Criteria.C7: Preserves available public annotations and explicitly marks unknown/ambiguous features instead of guessing.

MVP Criteria.C8: Evaluation set represents single CDS, multi-gene cassette, tagged fusion, and backbone-heavy constructs where public annotations allow.

MVP Criteria.C9: Compares the same pretrained model on intact and preprocessed benign constructs using a fixed version/configuration.

MVP Criteria.C10: Reports coverage, supported agreement/classification metrics, per-archetype results, runtime, and failure modes.

MVP Criteria.C11: Tests, environment/configuration, CLI, README, and a benign end-to-end demo are included.

MVP Criteria.C12: No model training/fine-tuning, proprietary/customer data, hazardous sequence collection, generative completion, or production deployment.

MVP Criteria.C13: Fragment completion, sub-segment reference indexing, red-team evaluation, and public benchmark release are not required for the four-week MVP.
